extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying to Alzheimer's Research UK grant schemes (dementia/Alzheimer's researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of eligibility, focus, and evaluation criteria for applying to Alzheimer’s Research UK funding schemes, including scheme-specific eligibility and priorities (e.g., translational potential, career-stage awards, pilot-to-major progression).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with Alzheimer's Research UK remit
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must fall within Alzheimer’s Research UK’s remit which covers biomedical research in Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that do not address biomedical research in Alzheimer’s disease or other dementias are out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research focus: treatment, diagnosis and prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Alzheimer’s Research UK funds research into treatment, diagnosis and prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is intended for projects that address these specific areas of dementia research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Of particular importance is research which has translational potential to benefit people with or at risk of dementia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes basic preclinical as well as clinical research that could lead to real-world benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: care or service delivery research
rubrics_metrics.description: This includes basic preclinical as well as clinical research, but not care or service delivery research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects focused on care models, service delivery, or health service operations are not eligible under this remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant applications are awarded on the basis of scientific merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be rigorously reviewed for the quality, rigor and significance of the science proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for the scheme applied for
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant applications are awarded on the basis of suitability for the scheme applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select the scheme that matches their career stage, project scale and aims; misalignment with scheme purpose can affect funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open competition / comparative assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant applications are awarded on the basis of open competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are competitive; proposals are assessed relative to other submissions in the same call/scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Clinical Fellowship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Clinical Fellowship: For clinicians who’ve delivered previous dementia research projects and have clear plans to establish their own research programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for clinician-researchers with prior dementia research experience and a plan to become an independent programme lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Career Researcher Bridge Fund purpose/eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Early Career Researcher Bridge Fund: This scheme aims to enable the retention of early career researchers in dementia research or to address particular pinch points in their career path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at early-career researchers facing career transitions or short-term funding gaps; proposals should justify how funding will retain the researcher or address a specific career pinch point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspire Fund — public engagement focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspire Fund – public engagement grant: The Inspire Fund provides funding for projects that engage the public with the topic of brain health and reducing the risk of dementia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should be public engagement activities focused on brain health and dementia risk reduction rather than purely academic dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race Against Dementia Fellowship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Race Against Dementia Fellowship: For early-career scientists in their pursuit of innovative solutions to the big questions in dementia research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at early-career researchers proposing innovative approaches to major problems in dementia; emphasis on innovation and early-career status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot Projects: novelty and progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot Projects: Meant for novel research ideas that, if successful, would lead to a Major project or programme application to Alzheimer’s Research UK or other funding body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot awards should propose novel, exploratory work with clear potential to underpin a future larger application; success should plausibly lead to scale-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Projects: scale of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Projects: Meant for intermediate to large-scale research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for substantial projects requiring broader resources and scope than pilot studies; proposals should reflect intermediate-to-large scale aims and infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Research Fellowship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior Research Fellowship: For PhD-qualified researchers in transition to lead independent groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at researchers with a PhD who are moving toward independent group leadership; applications should demonstrate readiness to lead a research team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Fellowship eligibility (non-clinical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Fellowship: For PhD-qualified non-clinical researchers who have clear plans to establish their own research niche.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at non-clinical PhD holders with a defined plan to establish an independent research niche; applications should outline career development and research direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral Clinical Fellowships eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctoral Clinical Fellowships: For clinically qualified applicants wishing to develop a career that combines dementia research and professional practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for clinically qualified candidates seeking doctoral training that integrates research with continued clinical/professional practice.
